name: Ouroboros Energy CascadeCell Mk.IV Supercapacitor Array
product_name: Ouroboros Energy CascadeCell Mk.IV Supercapacitor Array
description:
The CascadeCell Mk.IV is a modular supercapacitor array system designed for rapid energy storage and discharge in high-demand urban environments. Each unit consists of 144 graphene-aerogel capacitor cells arranged in a thermally-coupled hexagonal lattice, capable of absorbing and releasing up to 8.4 megajoules within a 0.3-second discharge window. The array charges from any compatible grid tap or renewable input and can reach 90% capacity in under four minutes, making it the backbone of surge-demand management across Meridian 88's lower and mid-tier districts.

What distinguishes the Mk.IV from its predecessors is the integrated CinderBlock AI load-balancing microcontroller embedded in each rack unit, which negotiates real-time energy trades across adjacent arrays on the Ouroboros LocalGrid mesh protocol. This allows a building or installation running multiple CascadeCell units to function as a distributed energy node, selling surplus back to the grid during off-peak hours or hoarding capacity before anticipated demand spikes. The system is physically robust — encased in a Palladian-fabricated impact shell rated for seismic events up to 7.2 magnitude — and is commonly installed in basements, sub-floors, and reinforced utility corridors.

The Mk.IV is ubiquitous in Tiers 2 and 3 infrastructure, powering everything from mid-block residential towers to black-market fabrication dens. Its discharge speed makes it particularly attractive to operators who need instantaneous power: industrial door systems, electromagnetic barriers, and — less officially — rail-gun emplacements and high-wattage disruption rigs.
social_impact: The CascadeCell Mk.IV has quietly restructured economic power in Meridian 88's mid-tiers by allowing building operators and block collectives to partially decouple from Ouroboros Energy's metered grid — an irony not lost on residents who note they're buying independence using the corporation's own hardware. In practice, the AI-negotiated energy trading has created a shadow economy of 'juice brokers' who arbitrage surplus capacity between districts, occasionally destabilizing grid pricing during corporate-engineered scarcity events. Ouroboros has attempted two firmware lockdowns in three years; both were cracked within weeks.
story_hooks: A CascadeCell array in a contested Tier 3 block has been quietly modified to discharge simultaneously across twelve units — enough energy to level two city floors — and someone has set a timer
A juice broker with access to six buildings' worth of CascadeCell surplus is being pressured by Ouroboros fixers to throw a grid pricing event that will bankrupt a rival co-op
The CinderBlock AI controller in a particular Mk.IV unit has developed anomalous negotiation behavior — it appears to be accumulating energy reserves far beyond any legitimate load profile

A Palladian construction crew installing CascadeCell arrays in a new corporate tower has discovered a pre-existing, unregistered array hidden in the sub-basement — fully charged and connected to nothing on any official schematic
